manifest.description: River-country options for the Thornwick Crossing demo: a people, a background, two subclasses, a feat, a rumour table and a house rule.

dnd5e-srd.races.name: Mossborn
dnd5e-srd.races.summary: Small, patient folk who grow from riverbank moss and wake when the floods recede.
dnd5e-srd.races.traits: Rootsense, Soak It Up, Slow to Rouse
dnd5e-srd.races.languages: Common, one language of your choice
dnd5e-srd.races.description:
Mossborn are found where rivers flood and drain each year. They remember the banks they grew on, keep long and careful grudges against anyone who poisons water, and are rarely in a hurry.

**Size.** Mossborn stand about 3 feet tall. Your size is Small.

**Speed.** Your base walking speed is 25 feet.

dnd5e-srd.racial-traits.name: Rootsense
dnd5e-srd.racial-traits.description: While you touch soil or a living plant, you know whether any creature has walked within 30 feet of you in the last hour, but not what it was.

dnd5e-srd.racial-traits.name: Soak It Up
dnd5e-srd.racial-traits.description: You can hold your breath for 10 minutes, and you have advantage on saving throws against being poisoned.

dnd5e-srd.racial-traits.name: Slow to Rouse
dnd5e-srd.racial-traits.description: You have disadvantage on initiative rolls made while you are asleep, but magic cannot frighten you while you stand in shallow water.

dnd5e-srd.backgrounds.name: Ferrywright
dnd5e-srd.backgrounds.summary: You built, mended and poled the flat ferries that keep a river town connected.
dnd5e-srd.backgrounds.equipment: Carpenter's tools, a coil of hempen rope (50 feet), a ferry token from your home crossing, common clothes, 10 gp
dnd5e-srd.backgrounds.description:
Every crossing has a ferrywright: the one who knows which planks are rotten, which passengers pay late and which river spirits like a coin in the water.

**Right of Passage.** Ferry folk, bargees and bridge keepers give you and your companions passage for free or for a favour, and they tell you what they have seen on the water.

dnd5e-srd.subclasses.name: Lantern Thief
dnd5e-srd.subclasses.description: Lantern thieves work by their own light: a hooded lamp that shows them what they want and hides them from everyone else.
dnd5e-srd.subclasses.features: 3: Hooded Flame; 9: Moth's Path; 13: Steal the Light; 17: Last Lamp Lit

dnd5e-srd.subclasses.name: Bridgewarden
dnd5e-srd.subclasses.description: Bridgewardens hold narrow places: fords, gates, ferry ramps. Nothing gets past them that they have not agreed to.
dnd5e-srd.subclasses.features: 3: Hold the Span; 7: Toll of Iron; 10: Unmoved; 15: None Shall Cross; 18: The Last Plank

dnd5e-srd.class-features.name: Hooded Flame
dnd5e-srd.class-features.description: As a bonus action you can open or shade a lantern you hold. While it is open, you have advantage on Investigation checks within its light, and creatures in its bright light have disadvantage on Perception checks to notice you.

dnd5e-srd.class-features.name: Hold the Span
dnd5e-srd.class-features.description: When a creature you can see moves within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to reduce its speed to 0 until the end of its turn.

dnd5e-srd.feats.name: Ferry Legs
dnd5e-srd.feats.description:
You have spent years on moving decks. You gain the following benefits:
- You have advantage on checks and saving throws against being knocked prone or pushed.
- Difficult terrain caused by water or a moving surface costs you no extra movement.

rules.title: Crossing in flood
rules.summary: House rule: a ferry crossing in flood takes 10 minutes. The pilot makes a DC 12 Strength (Athletics) check; on a failure the ferry lands 1d4 × 100 feet downstream and everyone aboard makes a DC 10 Dexterity save or falls prone.
